6-Point Demand: Students of polytechnic instt resume protests
2025-04-28T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/6-point-demand-students-polytechnic-instt-resume-protests-3881606

Polytechnic students staged fresh demonstrations across the country yesterday, demanding urgent action on their six-point demand for reforms in technical education.

In Dhaka, students of Dhaka Polytechnic Institute brought out a procession in the Tejgaon area in the morning, moving through nearby roads before returning to the campus.

At the programme, Mashfik Islam, a movement representative, said similar protests were held across different regions without causing public inconvenience.

In a press release issued last night, students announced that protest processions would continue at polytechnic institutes nationwide.

Meanwhile, students of Rajshahi Polytechnic Institute continued their protest for the seventh consecutive day by locking the administrative building.

Salman Ahmed Tushar, a protester, said administrative buildings across all polytechnic institutes in Rajshahi remained locked and demonstrations would continue until demands were met.

Students of Rajshahi Mohila Polytechnic Institute and the Government Survey Institute also joined the protest.

Rajshahi Polytechnic Institute Principal Md Abu Hanif said administrative and academic activities were suspended due to the ongoing protests.

The fresh protests follow earlier demonstrations that began on April 16 and continued for several days.

The students' six-point demands include cancelling the 30 percent promotion quota for craft instructors, introducing a four-year standardised curriculum and an age limit for admissions, gradually shifting to English as the medium of instruction, enforcing reserved quotas for technical posts under Grade-10, and establishing a dedicated technical university for polytechnic and monotechnic graduates.

Students claim that these reforms are essential to ensure merit-based recruitment, strengthen technical education, and improve career prospects.
